questions.question: Which among the following is a protein-coding RNA?

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: Which of the following RNA is not directly involved in protein synthesis?
questions.explanation:
miRNA is not directly involved in protein synthesis. miRNA participates in the modulation of
gene expression by altering mRNA function.
The mRNAs, rRNAs, and tRNAs are directly involved in protein synthesis. Other RNAs participate
in either mRNA splicing (snRNAs) or modulation of gene expression by altering mRNA function
(mi/siRNAs) and/or expression (IncRNAs).

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: Which enzyme is responsible for the polymerization of ribonucleotides into a sequence complementary to the template strand of the gene?
questions.explanation:
DNA-dependent RNA polymerase is the enzyme responsible for the polymerization of
ribonucleotides into a sequence complementary to the template strand of the gene.
The enzyme attaches at a specific site, the promoter, on the template strand. This is followed by
the initiation of RNA synthesis at the starting point, and the process continues until a termination
sequence is reached.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: Which enzyme prevents the formation of superhelical tensions in the DNA during transcription?
questions.explanation:
Topoisomerase prevents the formation of superhelical tensions in the DNA during transcription.
During transcription, supercoils form when the DNA is unwound and can add stress to the
molecule. Topoisomerase activity enables RNA elongation to proceed further without being
stopped. This action of topoisomerase also takes place during DNA replication.

questions.question: RNA produced from a fragment of DNA has the sequence of UAAGGC. The sequence of the non-template strand in the DNA that gave rise to this sequence is which one of the following?
questions.explanation:
The non-template strand or coding strand in the DNA will have the same sequence of the RNA
that is produced, except that the non-template or coding strand has T is in place of U.
As all sequences are written in the 5’ to 3’ direction, unless otherwise specified, an RNA sequence
of UAAGGC would correspond to a DNA sequence, on the non-template strand, of TAAGGC. Both
the non-template strand and RNA produced will be a complementary sequence to the template
strand. Therefore, the template strand would be ATTCCG (written 5’ to 3’).

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about mRNA splicing is true?

options.text: The existence of split genes has no advantage
Self-splicing introns do not require the help of any protein for splicing to occur accurately
β-thalassaemia results from a genetic defect in the spliceosome

questions.correctAnswerText: Self-splicing introns do not require the help of any protein for splicing to occur accurately
questions.explanation:
Self-splicing introns do not require a spliceosome or any other proteins for the splicing reaction.
Self-splicing introns fold into complex loops and undergo transesterification reactions, thus
undergoing self splicing.
Other options:
Option A: Split genes have the advantage that they allow alternative splicing so that a single gene
can code for variant forms of the same protein.
Option C: B-thalassemia results from the faulty splicing of the B-globin transcript. However, the
spliceosome is normal and the reason for the fault is a mutation in the B-globin gene itself.
Option D: Splicing occurs in the nucleus and mature transcripts are then transported into the
cytosol for translation (protein synthesis) to occur.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: Which statement best explains the function of eEF-2?

options.text: It is required for the translocation of peptidyl-tRNA during translation
It is required for the initiation of protein synthesis
It is the agent that binds to, and is inactivated by, chloramphenicol
It functions as a peptidyl transferase

questions.correctAnswerText: It is required for the translocation of peptidyl-tRNA during translation
questions.explanation:
Eukaryotic elongation factor 2 (eEF-2) is required for the translocation of peptidyl-tRNA along the
mRNA during translation.
The elongation reaction requires GTP hydrolysis. The corresponding elongation factor in bacteria
is EF-G. Diphtheria toxin ADP-ribosylates eEF-2, leading to its inactivation.
Other options:
Option B: Initiation of eukaryotic protein synthesis requires several initiation factors, designated
elF-1, eIF-2, etc.
Option C: Chloramphenicol inhibits prokaryotic peptidyl transferase.
Option D: Peptidyl transferase is an rRNA (within the large ribosomal subunit) involved in
formation of the peptide bond between the amino acid groups within the A and P sites of the
ribosome.
